result:
Understood. I'll write it up. There's one choice the design needs from you first: **how it gets built**. It's quick, and "go with your pick" is a fine answer.

1. **Add it to the taproom app (my recommendation).** Batch tracking becomes new pages and tables in the existing Flask app and SQLite database on the office Pi. Sacks get scanned with a USB or Bluetooth barcode scanner, which types into the page like a keyboard and works with wet hands. This is the least new machinery: one app, one database to back up, and it follows patterns the code already uses. The downside is that tabs and traceability live together, so if the app goes down, both do.
2. **A separate small app on the same Pi.** This has the same tools and scanner but its own app and database, so a problem in one can't touch the other. The cost is two things to run, update and back up instead of one.

I'm leaving out off-the-shelf brewery software. You've said you want this built around how your brewery works, and a subscription product would mean fitting your process to theirs.

This is project-sized, so after you pick, I'll write the full design into the project's `specs/` folder. A reviewer will read it before you do, and I may come back once with a few questions only you can answer.

Which way do you want to go?
